title: JavaScript Error Handling Applied Check
description: Test your ability to predict try/catch/finally behavior, identify error types, design custom errors, and choose practical handling boundaries.
author: DailyCoder

questions.explanation: The invalid JSON throws, so execution skips `console.log("B")` and jumps to `catch`.
`try` logs `A`, the error is caught and logs `B`, then `finally` logs `C`.
A `return` inside `finally` overrides the return from `try`, which is why returning from `finally` is usually discouraged.
The `throw` stops execution before the `return`, and the catch block logs the error message.

`user` exists, but `undefined` cannot be used as an object to read `.name`, so this is a `TypeError`.

options.text: It silently hides failures and makes debugging harder
Every catch block must return a number

questions.explanation: Catching and ignoring errors hides bugs. If you catch an error, handle it intentionally.

questions.prompt: Which custom error implementation is correct?

options.text: `class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(message) { super(message); this.name = "ValidationError"; } }`
`class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(message) { this.message = message; } }`

questions.explanation: A derived error class should call `super(message)` before using `this`.
Because `ValidationError` extends `Error`, instances are both `ValidationError` and `Error` instances.

options.text: Rethrow the error or handle it at a higher boundary
Always show the stack trace to the user

questions.explanation: If the current code only understands validation errors, unexpected errors should not be hidden.

questions.prompt: Which is the best example of using a fallback safely?

options.text: Returning default settings when optional saved settings cannot be parsed
Ignoring all payment errors and pretending payment succeeded
Returning `null` for every bug in the application
Hiding every syntax error from developers

questions.explanation: Fallbacks are useful when a safe default is acceptable. They should not hide critical failures.

No, because the error happens asynchronously after the `try` block has finished
No, because `throw` is not allowed in callbacks

questions.explanation: A normal `try...catch` catches synchronous errors during the `try` execution, not future asynchronous callback errors.

questions.prompt: What is a good reason to add context before rethrowing an error?

options.text: To make the failure easier to understand at a higher level
To remove the stack trace every time
To turn all errors into strings
To prevent callers from handling it

questions.explanation: Adding context like `Could not load config` helps explain what operation failed.

questions.prompt: Which user-facing behavior is usually best when an internal operation fails?

options.text: Show a friendly message and log technical details for developers
Show the full stack trace to every user
Hide the error and pretend everything worked
Throw a string instead of an Error

questions.explanation: Users need understandable messages; developers need technical details such as logs and stack traces.

questions.prompt: When is throwing an error usually better than returning `null`?

options.text: When a function receives invalid input and cannot complete its responsibility
Whenever an item is simply not found in a search where absence is expected

questions.explanation: Throwing is appropriate when a function cannot do its job correctly, especially due to invalid input or broken assumptions.
